note: Pegunigalsidase alfa (approved 2023) and three alpha-Gal A gene therapies (ST-920, FLT190, AVR-RD-01) all ran through the Gla-knockout Fabry mouse; only the enzyme has an efficacy comparison and approval.

engagement.short: PRX-102 cleared tissue Gb3 in mice
engagement.quote: The repeat administration of the enzyme to Fabry mice caused significant reduction (p-value<0.05) of Gb3 in various tissues

NCT01678898 results posted 2020-01-27.
engagement.note: In the phase 1/2 trial pegunigalsidase alfa cut renal peritubular capillary Gb3 inclusions 84% in classic Fabry patients, as tissue Gb3 clearance in mice predicted.
engagement.short: Renal Gb3 fell in patients, as in mice
engagement.quote: All 11 male and 1 of 7 female patients presented with classic FD phenotype, in whom renal peritubular capillary Gb3 inclusions were reduced by 84%.
engagement.reason: Renal Gb3 cleared as mice predicted
engagement.judgement: Paired by me (comparison_stated false). Gb3 is the enzyme's own substrate, read as proximal. The mouse kidney cleared less (64% residual) than human PTC inclusions (-84%), so direction only. Gene-therapy members reproduced the pattern (ST-920, FLT190, AVR-RD-01: plasma alpha-Gal A and lyso-Gb3 in mice and in patients) without changing the status, so no extra entries.

engagement.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells

engagement.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. NCT02800070 has no results posted (registry checked). Paired by us: Huang 2017 is the model side (LV/AGA-transduced patient CD34+ cells in NSF mice). Year from https://www.theavrobio.org/avrobio-reports-six-month-data-showing-first-patient-treated-fabry-disease-achieved-normal-plasma-enzyme-activity-avr-rd-01-gene-therapy/ (tier 5, read in full); Khan 2021 stays the source of the status.
engagement.note: In FACTs (NCT02800070, LV/AGA, the vector later licensed as AVR-RD-01) all five men reached near-normal alpha-Gal A within a week, as the NSF xenograft predicted. First public in an AVROBIO press release (12 Oct 2017): the first FACTs patient reached normal plasma alpha-Gal A within 45 days.
engagement.short: Patients made alpha-Gal A, as predicted
engagement.quote: All patients produced α-gal A to near normal levels within one week.
engagement.reason: Enzyme activity rose in all patients
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison; model and trial used the same LV/AGA construct, which is the voxeralgagene autotemcel lineage. Direction only, as mouse and human assays differ.

engagement.model: Gla-knockout Fabry mice given clinical-scale ST-920 (AAV2/6 liver-directed hGLA) in a 3-month pharmacology/toxicology study

engagement.model: Gla-knockout Fabry mice given clinical-scale ST-920 (AAV2/6 liver-directed hGLA) in a 3-month pharmacology/toxicology study

Paired by us. Year from Sangamo press release 2021-11-04 (https://investor.sangamo.com/news-releases/news-release-details/sangamo-therapeutics-announces-preliminary-phase-12-data-showing), tier 5, read in full.
engagement.note: In STAAR every ST-920 dose group raised plasma alpha-Gal A activity at weeks 24 and 52, as the mouse study predicted. First public in Sangamo's 4 Nov 2021 release: all four patients in the first two cohorts had above-normal alpha-Gal A. Single-arm dose-ranging trial.
engagement.short: Patients' plasma alpha-Gal A rose, as predicted
engagement.quote: Change in alpha Gal-A activity in plasma from baseline at specific time points over the 1-year study period.
engagement.reason: Plasma enzyme rose in all dose groups
engagement.judgement: Mouse study ran before the 2019 trial start (IND-enabling), so prospective. Direction only; mouse and human assays differ.

dose.magnitude_basis: NOAEL AUC multiple of the MRHD (1.9-4.2x) vs the dose used (1x MRHD)
dose.confidence_note: Model side and human AUC both from the FDA multidisciplinary review; tolerability at 1 mg/kg from BALANCE and F01/02.
dose.model: Six-month IV toxicology, mice and cynomolgus monkeys (pegunigalsidase alfa)
dose.note: Six-month mouse and monkey studies were clean (immune reactions aside) at 1.9x and 4.2x the 1 mg/kg human AUC; patients were dosed to 1 mg/kg without such toxicity. Retrodiction: the toxicology was first public in the 2023 FDA review, after pegunigalsidase alfa's own patient safety and dosing results (phase 1/2, Schiffmann 2019), so it reproduces a known result.
dose.quote: No adverse effects were observed in mice or monkeys at doses up to 1.9x and 4.2x, respectively, the MRHD, based on AUC comparison.
dose.reason: Stated margin held at clinical dose
dose.judgement: Judgement call: the model stated a tolerability margin (NOAEL at 1.9x/4.2x MRHD by AUC) but no efficacy exposure target, so dose is scored on the margin half only. Patients got 1 mg/kg q2w (BALANCE, F01/02) with no non-immune dose-limiting toxicity. FDA excluded animal allergic reactions from the NOAEL as not predictive of human immunogenicity. Dated 2023, when the review made the margin public.

dose.magnitude_basis: predicted plasma alpha-Gal A in the normal range (4.0-21.9 nmol/h/mL) at 7.5e11 vg/kg vs patient 2 mean 3.9 and patient 1 about one-fifth of that
dose.confidence_note: Model side read in full (PMC10284695, epub 2023-01-11). Patient side tier 5: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2021/11/09/2330851/0/en/freeline-reports-new-data-from-fabry-disease-program-pipeline-and-company-updates-including-appointment-of-pamela-foulds-md-as-chief-medical-officer-and-third-quarter-2021-financia.html (cutoff 2021-10-06). Patient 1 level inferred from "Patient Two saw a 400% increase in enzyme levels compared with Patient One". Escalation stopped for business reasons (registry why_stopped).
dose.note: Mouse modelling and NHP scaling set 7.5e11 vg/kg to give normal-range plasma alpha-Gal A; Freeline's Nov 2021 release had patient 2 at 3.9 nmol/h/mL and patient 1 four-fold lower. Retrodiction: published 2023, after those results. The NHP tolerability margin was broken (liver enzymes, myocarditis); that harm is counted in safety.
dose.short: Starting dose fell short of normal enzyme
dose.quote: This dose was informed by the murine modelling of plasma α-Gal A activity levels required for Gb3 clearance and linear scaling to dose from NHP data to provide α-Gal A activity in plasma within the normal range
dose.judgement: The 2023 paper states an exposure target (normal-range plasma alpha-Gal A at the starting dose), scored on the NHP scaling track that stated it. It postdates FLT190's own patient enzyme data (Nov 2021), so it is a retrodiction; it did not reproduce them (one patient just under, one well under the normal range), so contra.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: renal Gb3: mouse kidney residual 64% vs patient PTC inclusions -84%
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. FDA nonclinical reviewers (BLA 761161, 2023) judged the mouse Gb3 data nonspecific: TLC with primuline staining 'was nonspecific and nonquantitative', so the model side is weaker than the paper claims. FDA accepted renal Gb3 (F01/02) as primary evidence and BALANCE eGFR as confirmatory.
efficacy.note: Renal PTC Gb3 inclusions fell 84% on pegunigalsidase alfa; BALANCE later showed eGFR slope non-inferior to agalsidase beta. Design: F01/02 was an open-label single-arm trial whose registered primary was adverse events; the renal PTC Gb3 endpoint FDA relied on governs. BALANCE (outcome) was a non-inferiority eGFR-slope trial against agalsidase beta.
efficacy.short: Renal Gb3 cleared; eGFR non-inferior later
efficacy.quote: All 11 male and 1 of 7 female patients presented with classic FD phenotype, in whom renal peritubular capillary Gb3 inclusions were reduced by 84%.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call on the endpoint: F01/02's registered primary was adverse events, so the efficacy endpoint FDA relied on (renal PTC Gb3, BLISS) governs as the PoC gate. The mouse predicted the surrogate, so outcome_tested comes from BALANCE (eGFR slope non-inferior to active agalsidase beta, -2.51 vs -2.16), scored positive though it is a non-inferiority result, not a placebo win. The mouse shows no renal decline, so it predicted nothing about eGFR itself.

patient_trials.quote: Based on rate of eGFR decline over 2 years, pegunigalsidase alfa was non-inferior to agalsidase beta.
reductions in plasma and urine globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) and globotriaosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb3) are seen.

efficacy.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results record: outcome typed PRIMARY in results; mean change -3.555 (range -4.020 to -3.090), only 2 analysed; trial terminated when AVROBIO dropped Fabry. Model side Huang 2017 abstract. Year from the AVROBIO release "87% Substrate Reduction in First Kidney Biopsy" (tier 5), dated July 2019 from search listings and its LinkedIn share; release text not read. efficacy.note: FAB-201 (AVR-RD-01): kidney PTC Gb3 inclusions fell by 3.6 per capillary at week 48 (n=2, registered primary), matching the xenograft's kidney Gb3 clearance. Design: open-label single-arm trial with no success bar set in advance, scored on its primary endpoint (kidney PTC Gb3 inclusions) against the predicted fall. First public in AVROBIO's July 2019 release of an 87% Gb3 reduction in the first kidney biopsy.
efficacy.short: Kidney Gb3 inclusions fell, as predicted
efficacy.quote: Healthy renal tissue would have no Gb3 inclusions. A reduction from baseline is desirable.
efficacy.reason: Kidney Gb3 fell in two patients
efficacy.judgement: The results record lists kidney PTC Gb3 change as a primary outcome alongside AEs, so endpoint_role primary; n=2 keeps confidence medium.

safety.magnitude_basis: presence vs absence of non-immune organ toxicity
safety.confidence_note: Both sides read from the same FDA review; one immune-complex glomerulonephritis case is also immune-mediated.
safety.model: Six-month IV toxicology, mice and cynomolgus monkeys (pegunigalsidase alfa)
safety.note: Animals showed no organ toxicity beyond immune reactions; patients' harms were hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis, which FDA treats as outside what animals predict. Retrodiction: the toxicology was first public in the 2023 FDA review, after pegunigalsidase alfa's own patient safety and dosing results (phase 1/2, Schiffmann 2019), so it reproduces a known result.
safety.short: No organ toxicity, as animals showed
safety.quote: The safety profile of PRX-102 is generally consistent with that of other enzyme replacement therapies. The main safety concern is the risks of severe hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, and infusion-associated reactions.
safety.reason: Silence held; immune harms out of scope
safety.judgement: Judgement call: animal allergic reactions to a human enzyme were excluded by FDA as 'not considered relevant to predicting potential immunogenicity in humans', so the species could not show the boxed-warning harm and its silence is no miss. The non-immune silence held.

safety.magnitude_basis: NHP clean at 3e13 vg/kg vs myocarditis and liver-enzyme rise at 7.5e11 vg/kg (40x lower)
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC10284695, epub 2023-01-11). Patient side tier 5: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2021/11/09/2330851/0/en/freeline-reports-new-data-from-fabry-disease-program-pipeline-and-company-updates-including-appointment-of-pamela-foulds-md-as-chief-medical-officer-and-third-quarter-2021-financia.html ("consistent with mild and transient myocarditis"; patient 2 had no liver-enzyme rise "under our current immune management regimen, which has evolved in response to patient data").
safety.note: NHPs at up to 3e13 vg/kg showed no FLT190-related toxicity, published Jan 2023 after Freeline had reported a liver-enzyme rise in patient 1 and mild myocarditis in patient 2 (Nov 2021). Retrodiction that failed to reproduce them.
safety.short: NHPs clean after patients' harms were public
safety.quote: In NHPs, α-Gal A expression was consistent with the levels of hGLA mRNA in liver, and no FLT190-related toxicities or adverse events were observed.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction rule for safety: FLT190's own patient harms were public (Freeline release, 2021-11-09) before the NHP silence was published, so the 2023 entry is a retrodiction; the NHPs did not reproduce the harms, so contra. NHPs can show AAV transaminase rises, so the silence is a miss.

safety.magnitude_basis: NHP clean at 3e13 vg/kg vs transaminase rise at 0.75e12 and 1.5e12 vg/kg (20-40x lower)
safety.confidence_note: Registry results table, not prose: the quote is the verbatim serious-adverse-event term (1 participant in each of the 0.75e12 and 1.5e12 vg/kg arms; 'Myocarditis' in 1), not a sentence. Trade press (fabrydiseasenews) reports the first patient's liver enzymes were treated with methylprednisolone and tacrolimus.
safety.note: MARVEL-1 results: serious transaminase increase in both dose cohorts and one myocarditis, at doses 20-40-fold below the clean NHP dose. Registry results confirm the 2023 contra with a tier 3 record.
safety.short: Patients' liver enzymes rose; NHPs silent
safety.judgement: NHPs can show AAV-related transaminase rises, so their silence is a miss: contra on the gene-therapy platform track. Paired by me; the registry posting (2026-08-06) is the first tier 1-3 record. Myocarditis counted with it.

safety.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
safety.note: GLP-style toxicology in NSF mice xenotransplanted with the LV/AGA cell product found minimal untoward effects; supported the Health Canada CTA.
safety.quote: Additional toxicology studies employing NSF mice xenotransplanted with the therapeutic cell product demonstrated minimal untoward effects.
safety.judgement: Opening safety entry at the first public statement of the tox study; FACTs had started in 2016 but reported no safety data until 2021.

safety.model: NOD/SCID/Fabry (NSF) mice xenotransplanted with lentivirus (LV/AGA)-transduced human CD34+ cells
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Confirmed later by NCT03454893 results (2024-01-05): no SAEs considered related to AVR-RD-01, no aberrant clonal expansion, no RCL. Year from the AVROBIO 2017-10-12 press release (tier 5), which postdates Huang 2017 (epub 2017-05-12), so the model stays prospective.
safety.note: No serious adverse events attributable to the LV/AGA cell product in five patients; conditioning-related events only, as xenograft toxicology predicted. First public in the 12 Oct 2017 AVROBIO press release: no study-related serious adverse events in the first six months.
safety.quote: No serious adverse events (AEs) are attributable to the investigational product.
safety.judgement: Paired comparison; xenograft silence on insertional or product toxicity held over follow-up so far. Conditioning (melphalan/busulfan) harms are outside the model.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no ST-920 NHP toxicology is public.
safety.note: The ST-920 mouse pharmacology/toxicology study reported a good safety profile; no patient safety results public yet.
safety.quote: Further optimization of vector design identified the clinical lead vector, ST-920, which produced several-fold higher plasma and tissue α-Gal A activity levels with a good safety profile.
safety.judgement: Opening safety entry for the ST-920 product track.

safety.model: Gla-knockout Fabry mice given clinical-scale ST-920 (AAV2/6 liver-directed hGLA) in a 3-month pharmacology/toxicology study
safety.confidence_note: Registry: serious TEAEs 3/33 (sepsis, brain stem stroke/CVA, chest pain, enthesopathy), none hepatic; non-serious transaminase/LFT rises in one female-group patient; related TEAEs common but none serious hepatic. Relatedness of SAEs not given. Year from Sangamo press release 2021-11-04 (https://investor.sangamo.com/news-releases/news-release-details/sangamo-therapeutics-announces-preliminary-phase-12-data-showing): "no treatment-related serious adverse events. No patients experienced liver enzyme elevations requiring steroid treatment."
safety.note: In STAAR (up to 2.63e13 vg/kg) no hepatic or other product-type serious harm appeared; SAEs were sepsis, stroke, chest pain and enthesopathy, as the clean mouse study predicted. First public in Sangamo's 4 Nov 2021 release: no treatment-related serious adverse events and no liver enzyme rise needing steroids.
safety.short: No serious product-type harm, as predicted
safety.quote: All incidences of serious Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs) in subjects who receive ST-920 as assessed by Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE)
safety.reason: No serious hepatic harm in 33 patients
safety.judgement: Silence held: unlike FLT190 there was no serious transaminase event; the SAEs are Fabry-type or intercurrent events a mouse could not show. Medium because SAE relatedness is not posted.
